slides.title: This one takes ==15 seconds==. If you see it.

slides.stem: The function f is defined by `f(x) = 3x − 7`. If `f(a) = f(2a − 5)`, what is the value of a?
slides.hand: time yourself — answer in the comments

slides.body: The 15-second version: a line with slope 3 never repeats an output. So if f(a) and f(2a − 5) are equal, the inputs must be equal. Set a = 2a − 5 and you get a = 5. No expanding, no distributing.

slides.title: Same output means same input
slides.body:
Any linear function with a nonzero slope hits each output exactly once. So whenever the SAT sets f(one thing) equal to f(another thing), skip the algebra and set the two inputs equal.

This shows up about once per test, usually late in Module 2 where time is tightest.
